name: Ulvestad Variation — White Tactics
description: 4 tactical challenges for White in the Ulvestad Variation. Find the winning 2-move sequence to exploit the active Black knights and seize the initiative.

drills.name: Black plays c3
drills.description: White to play. After 7...Nxd5, deviate with 8.cxd4! instead of the main line 8.Ne4.
drills.explanation: Black to move. No forced tactic exists here, but c3 is clearly the strongest continuation. Line: 1. c3 Nxd5 2. cxd4 Qxg5 3. Bxb5+. Stockfish 18 (depth 16) evaluates the result at +0.39 for Black, 1.11 pawns better than the next-best alternative.

drills.name: Qa4+ Check
drills.description: Black to play. The engine's choice in this position: cxd4 (-0.44).
drills.briefExplanation: The strongest move is cxd4 (pawn to cxd4). 1. cxd4 exd4 2. Bb5+ Bd7 3. Bxd7+.
drills.explanation: Black to move. No forced tactic exists here, but cxd4 is clearly the strongest continuation. Line: 1. cxd4 exd4 2. Bb5+ Bd7 3. Bxd7+. Stockfish 18 (depth 16) evaluates the result at -0.44 for Black, 2.98 pawns better than the next-best alternative.

drills.name: Nxf6+: Blowing Open the Center
drills.description: White to play. Sacrifice the knight on f6 to shatter Black’s center, then strike with Bb5+.
drills.briefExplanation: Nxf6+! wrecks Black’s pawn shield; cxd4 opens the center and Bb5+ picks up the piece.
drills.explanation: Black to move. There is a real tactic here: Nxf6+ winning material. Line: 1. Nxf6+ Qxf6 2. cxd4 exd4 3. Bxb5+. Stockfish 18 (depth 16) evaluates the result at +2.81 for Black, 1.63 pawns better than the next-best alternative.
